extracted.intended_audience: Researchers invited to act as peer reviewers for F1000Research (academic reviewers)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines for researchers invited to review articles published on the F1000Research platform, describing the open post-publication peer review model, reviewer conduct, how to write reports, approval/status definitions, and article-type-specific review questions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer review model — identity transparency & openness
rubrics_metrics.description: F1000Research uses an open and transparent peer review model: identity transparency (all identities visible), reviewer interacts with editor/other reviewers/authors, review information published (review reports, submitted manuscript, reviewer identities), and post-publication commenting is open.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Peer review reports are published alongside reviewers’ full names and affiliations, remain attached to the article (including indexing), are citable and have a DOI. Reviewers should be aware their reports and identities will be public.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment focus — scientific validity over novelty
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers are asked to assess the scientific validity of the article, rather than the novelty or interest levels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The approval rating should be based on whether the reported findings or analyses are correct and valid, not on the novelty or importance of an article. Each article type has its own review focus/questions to assist with this.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open Data requirement for original results
rubrics_metrics.description: Articles discussing original results must make available the underlying source data alongside, and detail any software used to process them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers will be asked to comment whether the source data are appropriate for others to reproduce the work. F1000Research has an Open Data policy and checks data availability at pre-publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-publication check — eligibility to publish
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors must be active researchers (scientists, scholars or clinicians) and the research must have been carried out at a recognised institution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a pre-publication administrative check performed by the editorial team to ensure basic eligibility before peer review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-publication check — correct article type and format
rubrics_metrics.description: Articles are checked to ensure they meet the criteria and format of the specific article type submitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Different article types have different review questions and expectations; reviewers should consult the article-type-specific guidelines when assessing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-publication check — readability/language standard
rubrics_metrics.description: As F1000Research does not copy-edit articles, the standard of language and readability must be sufficient for readers to be able to follow the article.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a reviewer finds the language hinders understanding, they should comment on clarity and suggest improvements; editorial team may contact reviewers for clarification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-publication check — plagiarism screening
rubrics_metrics.description: Articles are checked for plagiarism before publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should alert editorial team if they identify suspected plagiarism missed by pre-publication checks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-publication check — methods details available
rubrics_metrics.description: Checks ensure that details of methods and resources are provided so the work can be assessed and reproduced.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers as experts should comment whether more information is required for others to reproduce the work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-publication check — adherence to ethical policies
rubrics_metrics.description: Articles publishing research involving humans or animals are checked to adhere to F1000Research ethical policies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should comment if ethical approvals or ethical reporting are missing or inadequate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-publication check — data availability verification
rubrics_metrics.description: Editorial checks confirm that source data underlying results are made openly available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers are asked to comment whether the provided source data are appropriate and sufficient for full reproducibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer eligibility — expertise & conflicts
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers are chosen to ensure they are experts in their field; for statistical analyses, reviewers with appropriate statistical knowledge are selected. Potential competing interests should be declared before starting a review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you have a competing interest contact the editorial team before writing the review; declare any competing interests when submitting your report for publication alongside your review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer reviewer code of conduct — read the full article
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers must read the full text of the article and view all associated figures, tables and data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Thorough reading is required to produce a considered report; partial reading is not acceptable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer reviewer code of conduct — be thorough
rubrics_metrics.description: A peer review report should discuss the article in full as well as individual points, and should demonstrate your understanding of the article.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reports should not be cursory; they should cover both high-level appraisal and detailed comments where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer reviewer code of conduct — be specific
rubrics_metrics.description: Comments should contain as much detail as possible, with references where appropriate, so the authors are able to fully address the issue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific, evidence-backed suggestions are preferred to vague criticism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer reviewer code of conduct — be constructive in criticism
rubrics_metrics.description: Include any concerns or criticisms in a constructive and respectful manner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Constructive feedback explains problems and suggests ways to address them rather than merely stating faults.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer reviewer code of conduct — avoid derogatory comments or tone
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure comments focus on scientific content rather than the authors; avoid derogatory remarks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Review as you wish to be reviewed; tone is important because reviews are published with reviewer identity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer reviewer code of conduct — be objective and impartial
rubrics_metrics.description: Focus your review on the academic content of the article itself and avoid being influenced by personal opinions of the article or the authors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Declare conflicts that might bias your view; opinions about authors should not affect scientific judgment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approval status — Approved
rubrics_metrics.description: No or only minor changes are required: aims and research methods are adequate; results are presented accurately; and the conclusions are justified and supported by the data or supporting material.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selecting 'Approved' indicates the work is valid and ready for indexing criteria (subject to editorial checks).

rubrics_metrics.name: Approval status — Approved with Reservations
rubrics_metrics.description: The reviewer believes the paper has academic merit, but has asked for a number of small changes to the article, or specific, sometimes more significant revisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use when the paper is fundamentally sound but requires revisions; published review should specify the reservations/required changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approval status — Not Approved
rubrics_metrics.description: The article has fundamental flaws that seriously undermine the findings and conclusions. It requires crucial substantial revisions for it to become academically valid.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select when methodological or other critical issues invalidate the main findings; explain the specific flaws and what is required to address them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Writing the review — clarity and quality of report
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviews should be understandable and well-written; the editorial team will request clarification if needed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Write clearly; if the editorial team needs further clarification they may contact the reviewer before publication of the review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Writing the review — include summary plus assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviews should be detailed offering a summary of the article under review as well as an assessment of its quality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a concise summary of aims and findings followed by evaluation of methods, results, interpretation, and data availability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Writing the review — base judgments on quality not novelty
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviews should not be based on novelty but on the quality of the article under review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even papers reporting single findings, replications, or null results are judged on validity; tailor comments to the article type.

rubrics_metrics.name: Writing the review — structure, constructive points, actionable feedback
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviews should be structured, constructive, and offer clear points for authors to address.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use headings or sections (e.g., summary, major issues, minor issues, data/code requests); the editorial team links to examples and tips for structuring reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Writing the review — citation requests must be justified
rubrics_metrics.description: Requests for citations of other articles should be justified and reviewers should explicitly state their reasoning when asking authors to cite their own work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not request citations for irrelevant or self-promotional reasons; explain why a suggested citation is necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allegations of misconduct — reporting route
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers should alert the peer review team (via provided email) if they wish to make an allegation of publication or research misconduct (e.g., plagiarism or image manipulation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide clear evidence or rationale when reporting suspected misconduct; follow editorial instructions for such allegations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Competing interest disclosure for published reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers who have any potential conflict of interest that would not disqualify them from reviewing should indicate this when submitting their review — competing interest declarations will be published alongside their review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be transparent about any relationships, funding, or other interests that could be perceived to influence the review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewers should re-review revised versions
rubrics_metrics.description: When authors revise their article in response to reviewer comments, the original reviewers are re-invited to review the new version and may publish an updated report taking revisions into account.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Updating your review is important to indicate whether concerns have been addressed satisfactorily; all versions and peer review reports remain published for transparency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indexing condition based on approval statuses
rubrics_metrics.description: Once an article receives two ‘Approved’ or two ‘Approved with Reservations’ status and one ‘Approved’ status, it will be indexed in PubMed and other bibliographic databases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Peer reviewer selections of approval statuses directly affect whether the article is indexed; reviewers should choose statuses that reflect validity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research Article review questions
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the work clearly and accurately presented and does it cite the current literature? Is the study design appropriate and does the work have academic merit? Are sufficient details of methods and analysis provided to allow replication by others? If applicable, is the statistical analysis and its interpretation appropriate? Are all the source data underlying the results available to ensure full reproducibility? Are the conclusions drawn adequately supported by the results?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these questions to structure assessment of primary Research Articles; focus on clarity, methods, data, statistics, and support for conclusions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Brief Report review questions
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the work clearly and accurately presented and does it cite the current literature? Is the study design appropriate and does the work have academic merit? Are sufficient details of methods and analysis provided to allow replication by others? If applicable, is the statistical analysis and its interpretation appropriate? Are all the source data underlying the results available to ensure full reproducibility? Are the conclusions drawn adequately supported by the results?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Brief Reports follow similar evaluation criteria to Research Articles; ensure brevity does not compromise reproducibility or clarity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Genome Notes review questions
rubrics_metrics.description: Are the rationale for sequencing the genome and the species significance clearly described? Are the protocols appropriate and is the work technically sound? Are sufficient details of the sequencing and extraction, software used, and materials provided to allow replication by others? Are the datasets clearly presented in a usable and accessible format, and the assembly and annotation available in an appropriate subject-specific repository?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess technical soundness, completeness of methods/software details, and appropriate data/repository deposition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Policy Brief review questions
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the paper provide a comprehensive overview of the policy and the context of its implementation in a way which is accessible to a general reader? Is the discussion on the implications clearly and accurately presented and does it cite the current literature? Are the recommendations made clear, balanced, and justified on the basis of the presented arguments?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasise clarity for non-specialist readers, accurate context, and justified, balanced recommendations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Case Studies review questions
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the background of the case’s history and progression described in sufficient detail? Is the work clearly and accurately presented and does it cite the current literature? If applicable, is the statistical analysis and its interpretation appropriate? Are all the source data underlying the results available to ensure full reproducibility? Are the conclusions drawn adequately supported by the results? Is the case presented with sufficient detail to be useful for teaching or other practitioners?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess completeness of case description and pedagogical or practical usefulness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Systematic Review review questions
rubrics_metrics.description: Are the rationale for, and objectives of, the Systematic Review clearly stated? Are sufficient details of the methods and analysis provided to allow replication by others? Is the statistical analysis and its interpretation appropriate? Are the conclusions drawn adequately supported by the results presented in the review?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate comprehensiveness of methods (search strategy, selection criteria), reproducibility, and appropriateness of synthesis/analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Software Tool Article review questions
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the rationale for developing the new software tool clearly explained? Is the description of the software tool technically sound? Are sufficient details of the code, methods and analysis (if applicable) provided to allow replication of the software development and its use by others? Is sufficient information provided to allow interpretation of the expected output datasets and any results generated using the tool?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check code availability, documentation, technical soundness, and clarity of expected outputs and usage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Method Article review questions
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the rationale for developing the new method (or application) clearly explained? Is the description of the method technically sound? Are sufficient details provided to allow replication of the method development and its use by others? If any results are presented, are all the source data underlying the results available to ensure full reproducibility? Are the conclusions about the method and its performance adequately supported by the findings presented in the article?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus on reproducibility, clarity of method, and adequacy of evidence for performance claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data Note review questions
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the rationale for creating the dataset(s) clearly described? Are the protocols appropriate and is the work technically sound? Are sufficient details of methods and materials provided to allow replication by others? Are the datasets clearly presented in a useable and accessible format?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess dataset documentation, accessibility, and technical validity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Study Protocol review questions
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the rationale for, and objectives of, the study clearly described? Is the study design appropriate for the research question? Are sufficient details of the methods provided to allow replication by others? Are the datasets clearly presented in a useable and accessible format?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether the planned design, methods, and outcomes are sufficiently specified for future replication and assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Case Report review questions
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the background of the case’s history and progression described in sufficient detail? Are enough details provided of any physical examination and diagnostic tests, treatment given and outcomes? Is sufficient discussion included of the importance of the findings and their relevance to future understanding of disease processes, diagnosis or treatment? Is the case presented with sufficient detail to be useful for other practitioners?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure clinical details are adequate and that discussion places the case in relevant clinical context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clinical Practice Article review questions
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the background of the cases’ history and progression described in sufficient detail? Are enough details provided of any physical examination and diagnostic tests, treatment given and outcomes? Is sufficient discussion included of the importance of the findings and their relevance to future understanding of disease processes, diagnosis or treatment? Is the conclusion balanced and justified on the basis of the findings?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess clinical relevance, thoroughness of reporting, and balance/justification of conclusions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correspondence review questions
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the rationale for commenting on the previous publication clearly described? Are any opinions stated well-argued, clear and cogent? Are arguments sufficiently supported by evidence from the published literature or by new data and results? Is the conclusion balanced and justified on the basis of the presented arguments?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check that commentary is evidence-based, focused, and balanced.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review article review questions
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the topic of the review discussed comprehensively in the context of the current literature? Are all factual statements correct and adequately supported by citations? Is the review written in accessible language? Are the conclusions drawn appropriate in the context of the current research literature?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate completeness, accuracy of claims and citations, and accessibility of exposition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opinion article review questions
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the topic of the opinion article discussed accurately in the context of the current literature? Are all factual statements correct and adequately supported by citations? Are arguments sufficiently supported by evidence from the published literature? Are the conclusions drawn balanced and justified on the basis of the presented arguments?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Opinion pieces should be accurate, evidence-aware, and balanced in conclusions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Registered Report — Stage 1 review questions
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the rationale for, and objectives of, the study clearly described? Is the study design appropriate for the research question (including statistical power analysis, where appropriate)? Are sufficient details of the methods provided to allow replication by others? Have the authors pre-specified sufficient outcome-neutral tests for ensuring that the results obtained can test the stated hypotheses, including positive controls and quality checks? Are the datasets clearly presented in a useable and accessible format?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess the pre-registration completeness, study design rigour, power considerations, and prespecified quality checks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Registered Report — Stage 2 review questions
rubrics_metrics.description: Are the data able to test the authors’ proposed hypotheses by satisfying the approved outcome-neutral conditions (such as quality checks, positive controls)? Are the introduction, rationale and stated hypotheses the same as the approved Stage 1 submission? (required) Did the authors adhere precisely to the registered experimental procedures? If not, has an explanation been provided regarding any change? Are any unregistered post hoc analyses added by the authors justified, methodologically sound and informative? Is the work clearly and accurately presented and does it cite the current literature? Is the study design appropriate and does the work have academic merit? Are sufficient details of the methods and analysis provided to allow replication by others? If applicable, is the statistical analysis and its interpretation appropriate? Are all the source data underlying the results available to ensure full reproducibility? Are the conclusions drawn adequately supported by the results?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stage 2 focuses on whether the registered plan was followed and whether outcomes meet pre-specified criteria; justify any deviations and evaluate analyses and reproducibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Book Chapter review questions
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the work clearly and accurately presented? Are all factual statements correct and adequately supported by citations to the current literature? Are any opinions stated well-argued, clear, and cogent? If applicable, are any methods and analyses appropriate and sufficiently detailed, to allow replication by others? If applicable, are the source data underlying the results available to ensure full reproducibility? Are the conclusions drawn appropriate and justified on the basis of the presented work? Is the work an appropriate addition to this book project, and does it align with the scope and/or objectives?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess clarity, factual accuracy, appropriate methods (when applicable), reproducibility, and fit with the book's aims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer selection & volunteering guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Volunteer reviewers should contact the editorial office, attach a CV and complete the reviewer form so the editorial team can confirm they meet the Reviewer Criteria. Reviewers are chosen to ensure they meet expertise requirements and may be invited for specific manuscripts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicate interest and provide evidence of expertise; selection is not guaranteed even if you volunteer.
